packs.name: Consumer web
packs.summary: Public-facing sites read by strangers: marketing pages, landing pages, product sites, documentation and editorial.
packs.summaryVi: Trang công khai cho người lạ đọc: trang marketing, landing page, trang sản phẩm, tài liệu và nội dung biên tập.
packs.optimisesFor: The first five seconds, for a stranger who arrived from a search result and owes you nothing.
when: a marketing site, landing page or product page
a pricing page, a documentation site or an editorial article
anything a stranger arrives at from a search result, an ad or a link
a request to look more premium, modern or trustworthy, or less generic
work judged on whether the reader keeps scrolling
notFor: internal tools, admin panels and operations consoles - use the erp pack, which is built for the opposite reader
dense data entry or any screen an operator works in all day
data tables that must show twenty or more rows at once
native mobile app interfaces, which have their own navigation conventions and touch targets

surfaces.chrome: minimal - a header that floats over the canvas rather than framing it
surfaces.canvas: warm off-white, or a dark section used deliberately for contrast
surfaces.content: the canvas itself; cards are used sparingly, not as the default container
surfaces.floating: menus and dialogs, generous radius, soft warm shadow
surfaces.accent: one saturated teal, reserved for the primary action
surfaces.semantic: success/warning/danger, used only in forms and system messages

overrides.rule: core/02-typography.md: one family, plus a monospace
overrides.why: Brand voice is a deliverable here, not a nice-to-have, and a display face is the cheapest way to stop a page reading as a template. The cost core names is real and is paid explicitly: both families are self-hosted, subset, preloaded and declared font-display: swap with metric-matched fallbacks, and the pairing is capped at two families total.

platform.note: Touch first: most strangers arrive on a phone. A pointer is the refinement, never the assumption.

packs.name: ERP & back-office
packs.summary: Dense, dark-chrome operational software: admin panels, operations consoles, back-office tools, internal dashboards.
packs.summaryVi: Phần mềm vận hành mật độ cao, chrome tối: admin panel, console vận hành, công cụ back-office, dashboard nội bộ.
packs.optimisesFor: The two-hundredth use by a trained operator, not the first impression.
when: an internal business tool, admin panel or operations console
a back-office screen or an operational dashboard
a request to look like a real ERP rather than a consumer SaaS
a screen that must stay readable through a full working day
notFor: marketing sites, landing pages or anything optimised for a first impression
consumer mobile apps - the density assumes a mouse and a large screen
content-first reading experiences - blogs, documentation, editorial
storefronts and product pages, where the product image is the subject

surfaces.accent: deep crimson #b3121b on light, #f2555e on dark
surfaces.semantic: success/warning/danger/info, danger pushed off the accent hue

platform.note: The density assumes a mouse and a full keyboard. On a touchscreen the row height and the hit areas are both wrong, and relaxing them relaxes the thesis.

packs.name: Immersive web
packs.summary: Public pages built around one real-time 3D scene the visitor can drive: product viewers and configurators, a 3D hero for a company site, a spatial subject taught in the browser - with three.js, React Three Fiber or model-viewer.
packs.summaryVi: Trang công khai dựng quanh một cảnh 3D thời gian thực mà khách tự điều khiển: xem và cấu hình sản phẩm, hero 3D cho trang doanh nghiệp, môn học có tính không gian - bằng three.js, React Three Fiber hoặc model-viewer.
packs.optimisesFor: The moment a stranger turns the object themselves - on a page that had already told them what it is before the scene arrived.
when: a product page where the visitor rotates, opens or configures the product in 3D
a company, studio or portfolio site whose hero is an interactive scene
a course or explainer page for a subject that is spatial - anatomy, mechanics, architecture, geography
a request for three.js, WebGL, WebGPU, React Three Fiber, model-viewer, a GLB embed or a scroll-driven 3D section
a question about whether something should be real-time 3D, a pre-rendered video or a still
a 3D page that is slow, hot, blank on a phone, or failing an accessibility or performance review
notFor: a marketing or landing page with no real-time scene - use the consumer-web pack, whose JavaScript budget this pack spends several times over
games and full-screen 3D applications - editors, CAD viewers, anatomy atlases a user works in for an hour; there the viewport is the product and the page-first rule here is wrong
internal tools, admin panels and dashboards - use the erp pack; a scene is decoration to an operator on their two-hundredth visit
installed mobile apps - use the mobile-app pack
a fixed camera fly-through nobody can steer - that is a video, and it should be shipped as one
charts and data visualisation, including 3D charts - core's chart rules cover them and a perspective axis breaks them
packs.density: low - 16px base, one scene per page, and at most one idea on the stage at a time

surfaces.chrome: minimal - a header floating over the stage, on an opaque plate once anything scrolls beneath it
surfaces.canvas: the stage: a near-black surface the scene is lit against, with a light page surface for long-form sections
surfaces.content: HTML in its own lane beside the scene, or on an opaque plate over it - never set directly on a moving render
surfaces.floating: plates, the option picker and hotspot popovers - one luminance step above the stage, no shadow
surfaces.accent: one blue with a value per surface, reserved for the primary action and the selected option
surfaces.semantic: success/warning/danger, in forms and scene status only

platform.note: Touch first, and touch is where a scene does the most damage: a canvas that takes every gesture is a hole in the page a thumb cannot scroll across. Vertical movement always belongs to the page.

packs.name: Mobile app
packs.summary: Installed apps held in one hand: iOS and Android, native or cross-platform, used in short interrupted sessions.
packs.summaryVi: Ứng dụng đã cài, cầm bằng một tay: iOS và Android, native hay cross-platform, dùng trong những phiên ngắn và hay bị ngắt quãng.
packs.optimisesFor: One thumb, on a screen that will be interrupted before the task is finished.
when: an installed app on a phone or tablet, native or cross-platform
a screen operated with a thumb rather than a cursor
a question about where a control belongs on a small screen
a screen that must survive being backgrounded, rotated or interrupted
porting a desktop or web screen down to a phone
notFor: desktop admin panels, operations consoles and anything used with a mouse at desk distance - use the erp pack
marketing sites and landing pages, even the ones read on a phone - use the consumer-web pack, which optimises for a stranger's first five seconds rather than for a returning user's thumb
dense data tables and any screen whose job is to show twenty rows at once
watch, TV and spatial interfaces, whose input and viewing distance are different problems again
packs.density: comfortable - 17pt/16sp body, 44pt minimum row height, 16pt screen margins

surfaces.chrome: the tab bar and the navigation bar - translucent over the content, flush with the system, never a frame around it
surfaces.canvas: the scrolling content itself; there is no separate page background behind it
surfaces.content: list rows separated by inset dividers, not cards
surfaces.floating: sheets that rise from the bottom edge - the dominant modal form; dialogs are the exception
surfaces.accent: one value per surface, and it marks the single primary action per screen
surfaces.semantic: success/warning/danger/info, with danger reserved for what cannot be undone

overrides.rule: core/03-layout.md: never remove functionality at a smaller size - change its form
overrides.why: A phone is not a smaller size of something, it is the only size. This pack removes functionality outright rather than compacting it: a secondary report, a bulk edit, a twelve-column table are moved to the web app and linked, because the compacted version of each one is worse than an honest absence. The core rule protects a responsive layout from dropping features as the viewport narrows; it is not a mandate to fit a desktop feature set onto a phone.

platform.note: One thumb, on a device held while walking. 44pt on iOS and 48dp on Android are the platform floors; this pack treats them as the floor and puts anything used often into the reachable arc at the bottom.
